business_problem: Oxide AI needed a more controllable and efficient way to turn large volumes of financial and market information into actionable investment insights without relying on opaque proprietary LLMs and fragmented cloud infrastructure.
solution_summary: Oxide AI piloted IBM watsonx.ai to power an investment-intelligence workflow that blends quantitative and qualitative information. The company’s product looks beyond traditional stock screeners by combining market data with research papers, patents, news feeds and social signals, but that breadth created operational pressure when using proprietary models and scattered infrastructure. With IBM Client Engineering, Oxide AI used watsonx.ai as a unified environment for generative AI and machine learning so it could test more transparent, task-specific models and regain control over deployment. In the resulting design, large financial corpora and market signals are analyzed inside watsonx.ai to generate candidate insights, while the company evaluates quality and response-time performance against prior baselines. The pilot reduced dependence on external black-box models, simplified implementation and gave Oxide AI a clearer path to stable, explainable AI-driven research workflows.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Provides the AI studio used to develop and run Oxide AI’s investment-intelligence workflow.

data_flow: Quantitative market data and qualitative sources such as patents, research papers, news feeds and social media are analyzed in watsonx.ai, where models generate research outputs that Oxide AI evaluates for quality and response performance.
business_outcome: Oxide AI improved model control and runtime performance while proving that watsonx.ai could support high-quality financial research outputs with less implementation complexity.
metrics: 37% faster average sequential response times than OpenAI GPT-4
